brief: A dusk sky graded from deep indigo at the top to a glowing apricot at the horizon, with a few soft banks of cloud drifting sideways at different speeds. Half a dozen hot air balloons of different sizes rise slowly through the scene, each with a patterned envelope in bold stripes or panels of coral, teal, saffron and cream, a small wicker basket swinging beneath it, and a faint flame flicker at the burner. Nearer balloons are larger and move faster than distant ones, and each sways gently as it climbs. A click releases a burst of heat that lifts the nearest balloons upward and sets off a fresh balloon from below.
statement: I wanted the quiet of watching balloons at the end of a day: a sky that shades from indigo to apricot, a few faint stars, and a handful of striped envelopes climbing at different paces so the nearer ones feel close and the far ones feel hazy. Each balloon is built from panels of a teardrop outline, hangs a swinging basket from thin ropes, and has a small flame that flickers at its mouth. Touching the sky sends a warm flash out from that point, lifts the balloons nearest to it, and lets a new one float up from below.
